From 468a272ca49cc4e2f58f3c360643c3f6d313c146 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2021 17:22:25 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: max98373-sdw: add missing memory allocation check

We forgot to test that devm_kcalloc doesn't return NULL.

Fixes: 349dd23931d1 ('ASoC: max98373: don't access volatile registers in bias level off')
Signed-off-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Guennadi Liakhovetski <guennadi.liakhovetski@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Bard Liao <bard.liao@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210607222239.582139-2-pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c b/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
index d8c47667a9ea..e178fdb6b899 100644
--- a/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
+++ b/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
@@ -786,6 +786,8 @@ static int max98373_init(struct sdw_slave *slave, struct regmap *regmap)
 	max98373->cache = devm_kcalloc(dev, max98373->cache_num,
 				       sizeof(*max98373->cache),
 				       GFP_KERNEL);
+	if (!max98373->cache)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < max98373->cache_num; i++)
 		max98373->cache[i].reg = max98373_sdw_cache_reg[i];
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `max98373-sdw.c`**
- Added a check after the memory allocation using `devm_kcalloc` to ensure that the allocation was successful. 
- If the allocation fails (i.e., if `max98373->cache` is NULL), the function now returns `-ENOMEM`, indicating an out-of-memory error.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a bug where the code did not previously check if the memory allocation for `max98373->cache` was successful. This oversight could lead to dereferencing a NULL pointer, potentially causing a crash or undefined behavior. The added check ensures that the function can gracefully handle memory allocation failures, improving the robustness of the code. The patch is linked to a previous commit that introduced the issue, thus providing a direct fix for that specific problem.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
max98373->cache = devm_kcalloc(dev, max98373->cache_num,
			       sizeof(*max98373->cache),
			       GFP_KERNEL);
```
Reason:
The `devm_kcalloc` function allocates memory for `max98373->cache`, but there is no subsequent check for a NULL return value. If the memory allocation fails, `max98373->cache` will be NULL, and any further attempt to access this uninitialized pointer will lead to dereferencing a NULL pointer, resulting in a crash or undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!max98373->cache)
	return -ENOMEM;
```
Reason:
This added check verifies whether `max98373->cache` is NULL after the memory allocation. If it is NULL, the function returns an error code (-ENOMEM) immediately, preventing any further code execution that would use the NULL pointer. This ensures that the program only proceeds when the memory allocation is successful.
